newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- Cash quiet but firm.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- Cash quiet but firm.

text.p: U.S. Municipal bonds were firm in early trade, while U.S. Treasuries were up 3/8 despite a big drop in weekly jobless claims.
"The market has a fairly good tone, there's just not a lot going on right now," one trader said. "It's not in rally mode, but it's just got a very definitely good tone."
Players were impressed with the overall success of Wednesday's deals, the trader said.
"There's a couple of national deals that probably could have done a little bit better, but I think the prices paid (overall) were just astronomical," he said.
Earlier Thursday, a trader said muni cash was starting to run "out of steam."

"I think the market's a little tired," he said. "We're seeing the beginning of some institutional selling. There's not a lot of bid wanteds out right now, but there's a couple of guys who want to sell bonds."
The trader had seen three lists so far, he said, the first of which totaled roughly $50 million.
"They'll definitely be some sellers in here today," he said.
A third trader said while munis may have looked a touch weaker early on, they were firm by mid-morning.
"It might have felt a little bit weaker first thing this morning, now the long bond is up 12 ticks," he said. "The market is actually better now than it was."

In the governments market, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was up 12/32 at 102-28/32 to yield 6.41 percent. The rise came despite news that jobless claims for the week ended July 19 fell 42,000 to 299,000, the lowest level in a year.
In debt futures, the September municipal contract was up 4/32 at 121-10/32. The September T-bond contract was 6/32 higher at 115-18/32. The MOB spread was 184 ticks.
